subject: Deployment fencing, network isolation, and threat Q&A — Edge inference
messages:
From: Simon Tate <simon.tate@zenithai.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@zenithai.com
Date: 2027-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP follow-up: network diagrams, isolation model, and threat summary

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the quick intake yesterday. As part of Zenith AI's vendor security review (RFP #ZEN-4532) we need the following artifacts to close our architecture appraisal:

- Logical network diagram for edge inference deployment (data flows between customer VPCs, sidecars, control plane, and telemetry egress)
- Tenant isolation model: process-level, network ACLs, and any workload fencing patterns you use
- Short threat-model summary (high-risk attack paths and mitigations) — 1-2 pages preferred
- Evidence or examples of egress controls and bastion/access patterns for private deployments

Can you provide the items above, preferably sanitized versions suitable for sharing with our procurement/security committee? If you prefer, a 30-min walkthrough next week will work.

We'd like to get this by Aug 25 if possible to keep the procurement timeline.

Best,
Simon Tate
Security Architect, Zenith AI
Simon.tate@zenithai.com

Attachments: Zenith_RFP_requirements_v3.pdf (ref)

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Simon Tate <simon.tate@zenithai.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-08-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: network diagrams, isolation model, and threat summary

Simon — thank you, and appreciate the clear list.

We're able to produce sanitized artifacts that address each bullet. Initial plan:

- I'll attach a redacted "edge_topology_v3" PDF that shows the logical flow and isolation boundaries.
- An "isolation_controls_matrix" CSV will map controls to customer-visible constructs (VPC peering, sidecar ACLs, KV cache scoping).
- A concise threat appendix (2 pages) that summarizes prioritized attack paths and compensating controls.

Marissa (cc), our Head of Security Architecture, will confirm whether we should include small config snippets (iptables/sidecar policies) or keep those as private evidence only. Vanessa will coordinate any evidence handoff/NDAs if needed.

Can you confirm the audience for the sanitized docs (procurement + security committee) and whether we should exclude any references to internal orchestration endpoints? We'll aim to get the sanitized bundle to you by end of day Aug 24. If that works, I'll also schedule a 30-min walkthrough for Aug 25 and send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com

Attachments (to follow): edge_topology_v3_sanitized.pdf (stub), isolation_controls_matrix.csv (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Simon Tate <simon.tate@zenithai.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-08-22T14:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: network diagrams, isolation model, and threat summary

Alex / Simon — quick clarifications from our side before we finalize the sanitized packet: 

1) Audience: if Zenith's security committee will see the artifacts, exclude any internal orchestration IPs and full hostnames. Provide abstracted CIDR ranges and role names (e.g., "control-plane-proxy") instead.

2) Evidence level: procurement generally accepts diagrams + matrices. Security may request config snippets or logs during the SOC/attestation phase. For now, provide:
   - diagram + control matrix (sanitized)
   - a short checklist mapping controls to evidence artifacts we can provide under NDA (firewall rules export, bastion access logs, egress ACL snippet)

3) Threat summary: include 3 prioritized attack paths and the primary mitigation for each (one-sentence mitigation + where it is enforced: sidecar, control plane, infra).

Alex — please ensure the isolation matrix includes: tenant identity boundaries, KV cache scoping, inter-pod sidecar policy, and any default-deny network posture. For the egress section: list permitted egress endpoints and the audit/logging retention policy.

Simon — if Zenith needs the config snippets ahead of the SOC review we can exchange them in a locked share (we'll propose a DocuSign/NDA page for that).

Marissa
Head of Security Architecture, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Simon Tate <simon.tate@zenithai.com>, procurement@zenithai.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-08-24T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: network diagrams, isolation model, and threat summary — packet delivered

Simon / team — attaching the sanitized packet per Marissa's guidance. Summary of contents below plus next steps.

Delivered artifacts (sanitized):
- edge_topology_v3_sanitized.pdf — logical diagram with abstracted role names, CIDR placeholders, and callouts for tenant fencing points
- isolation_controls_matrix.csv — mapping: control category, enforcement plane (sidecar/control-plane/infra), sample evidence label
- redwood-threat-scenarios-appendix.pdf — 2-page prioritized attack-paths and mitigations

Key highlights (TL;DR):
- Tenant fencing uses a combination of identity-scoped tokens, per-tenant KV namespaces, and per-request sidecar ACLs; default-deny at inter-pod and host level
- Egress: customer-configurable egress allowlist with forced egress via regional peering or customer-managed NAT; all egress flows are audited and long-term logs retained per contract (we noted our standard retention in the matrix)
- Fallbacks: compatible model-tiering for graceful degradation if a primary inferencing pool becomes isolated; automated routing policies in the control-plane (no customer data cached outside sanctioned caches)

Requested next steps:
1) Please confirm receipt and whether the sanitized level is acceptable for the committee.
2) If security wants config snippets or logs, indicate whether an NDA/DocuSign is required — we'll provision a locked share.
3) Proposed walkthrough: Aug 25 10:00–10:30 PT — I've sent a calendar invite to the listed contacts.

If you need us to redact further (e.g., remove regional zone labels), say so and we'll do a second pass.

Regards,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: edge_topology_v3_sanitized.pdf, isolation_controls_matrix.csv, redwood-threat-scenarios-appendix.pdf
